title: The Quiet Retaliation
notebook: Three procurement contracts in six weeks went to Arcturian-affiliated firms over cheaper Veltrian bids.
Approximately fourteen million kroner that should have gone to Veltrian firms.
The sub-ministry reports to a deputy minister Vael recommended eight months ago.
dialogue: Elara sets three documents on the desk. She does not speak until they are aligned precisely.
monologue: When Elara aligns documents before speaking, the numbers in them are the kind that do not improve on second reading.

narrative.text: Three procurement contracts in the last six weeks. All won by Arcturian-affiliated firms over Veltrian competitors who submitted lower bids. The evaluation committees in each case cited technical capacity assessments that I cannot verify — the underlying documentation was filed through a sub-ministry office that reports to a deputy minister Vael recommended for appointment eight months ago.

I cannot prove Vael is directing this. The chain of influence is indirect. What I can tell you is that the pattern is consistent and the amounts are not trivial — approximately fourteen million kroner in contracts that should have gone to Veltrian firms.
He told you he would compete like everyone else. He is competing. He is simply competing at a level that does not require him to bid.

vael_undermining_brief.monologue: He is competing at a level that does not require him to bid. Vyktor said it without inflection. That is his way of telling me I was naive when I thought rejection was a clean outcome.

choices.text: Refer the procurement irregularities to the BCA. If Vael is operating through a deputy minister, I want that documented.
Request a private meeting with Vael. Address this directly before it becomes a formal investigation.
Remove the deputy minister quietly. Do not escalate to a formal investigation — the political cost of a public confrontation with Vael outweighs the contracts.
